category.instructions: Classify what this DNS query exists to do. Judge the domain name, the record type, the response, and any repeat pattern as a whole.

criteria.infrastructure: Plumbing a device needs: CDNs, OS/app update and auth endpoints, time servers (fonts.gstatic.com, api.apple-cloudkit.com, ntppool.org).
criteria.normal-usage: Human-initiated browsing, apps, streaming, search, games (youtube.com, espn.com, roblox.com).
criteria.telemetry: Diagnostics, crash reports, usage pingbacks from apps or OS — not serving ads (telemetry.microsoft.com, crashlytics.com, app-measurement.com).
criteria.advertising: Ad servers, trackers, retargeting, RTB endpoints (doubleclick.net, adsrvr.org, graph.facebook.com when fetched by a tracker).
criteria.suspicious: Signals of bad intent: random-looking high-entropy names, brand lookalikes, odd TLDs with deep subdomains, or the same unknown domain queried at beacon-like regular intervals (xkjqwpzr.com, micros0ft-support.xyz).

suspicion.instructions: Rate how suspicious this single query is. Consider: entropy of the name, TLD reputation, brand-lookalike spelling, subdomain depth, whether the response is NXDOMAIN with a high repeat count, and whether any blocklist already flagged it.
criteria: 1: Benign — well-known domain, ordinary record type, nothing unusual anywhere in the record.
3: Routine — uncommon but plausible: long-tail sites, app backends, regional CDNs.
5: Notable — mixed signals: unusual TLD or deep subdomains but otherwise legitimate-looking; or a blocklist hit on an otherwise normal-looking name.
7: Suspicious — strong signals: high-entropy name, brand lookalike, or repeated lookups of a name that keeps failing or is blocklisted.
9: Critical — near-certain malicious infrastructure: DGA-style name, fresh NXDOMAIN pairings with high repeat counts, or known-bad patterns.

privacy.instructions: Decide whether this query could reveal sensitive personal information about a household member if it left the local network. Answer yes for private, no for not-private.

criteria.true: private: The domain or its pattern could reveal health, finance, identity, relationships, or intimate interests (medical portals, banking, dating, recovery/support resources, job hunting while employed).
criteria.false: not-private: No profiling-sensitive content is implied: shopping, sports, entertainment, OS plumbing, general browsing.

recommend.instructions: Recommend the next action. This system NEVER enforces on its own: suggest-block only queues a human approval. Match the recommendation to your own category and suspicion answers.

criteria.log-only: Suspicion 1-5: record it in the decision log and move on.
criteria.flag-review: Suspicion 7, or suspicious-category names that are plausibly legitimate: put it in the human review queue with a one-line rationale.
criteria.suggest-block: Suspicion 9, or repeated lookups of clearly malicious or lookalike names: propose a block that waits for explicit human approval before taking effect.
